sampling_model.design: The design algebra fixes any finite binary-path support \(\mathcal S\) and a positive ex ante reshaping law \(\Pi\); absorption is required only for the ordered Green, graph-rank, and adjacent-ratio corollaries.
sampling_model.units: Population identification uses i.i.d. triples \((X_i,W_i,Y_i)\) from \(P\).  A separate anchor-faithful estimator theorem uses the published possibly dependent unit-indexed triangular array and its maximal-correlation condition.
sampling_model.treatment: In the base algebra, \(W_i\) may be any path in the declared finite binary support.  Ordered adoption-time results explicitly restrict that support to absorbing paths.
sampling_model.overlap: The population layer assumes \(\pi_s(X)\geq c_{\pi}\) and \(\Pi_s\geq\epsilon\).  The published layer instead uses known unit-specific propensities \(\pi_i(s)\geq c_*\) on the reshaping support and defines its RIPW weight to be zero off that support.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The population functional uses a correct common generalized path propensity and pathwise conditional means.  The anchor-faithful statistical theorem is for the published known-propensity estimator; it does not assert a cross-fitted or doubly robust extension.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under their unit-indexed known-propensity setup, Assumptions 2.1--2.3, a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model, and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the corresponding average lag effect.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

body.tldr: For any finite binary-path support, a reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects, with covariance and pair-mass formulas, normalization, and exact rational diagnostics.  Under the distinct unit-indexed known-propensity conditions of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo, the corrected weighted regression with a grand intercept has the same tensor probability limit and exactly recovers their homogeneous Theorem \(4.1\).  For absorbing supports, graph connectivity gives the exact rank dimension and adjacent ratios give a pointwise Cramer sign certificate; a global classification of all sign chambers remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory establishes dynamic consistency under calendar-homogeneous effects and explicitly leaves its time-varying DATE equation beyond scope.  It permits arbitrary path support, unit-specific known propensities, and weak cross-unit dependence, so the present i.i.d. conditional-mean class is not a subclass comparison that can establish that theorem.  Existing event-study decompositions also do not provide the reshaped finite-memory calendar-by-lag tensor, an absorbing-support graph-rank law, or exact fixed-law sign certificates.
project_justification.niche: The missing objects are an arbitrary-path forward loading tensor shared across two clearly separated sampling layers, plus sharp ordered diagnostics that use absorption only where it is mathematically necessary.
project_justification.fill: The project proves arbitrary-path covariance and pair-mass identities, exact normalization and rational diagnostics, a positive-law absorbing graph formula for kernel dimension, and an anchor-faithful calendar-varying probability limit for the published estimator with its grand intercept.  It also supplies a fixed-law adjacent-ratio Cramer certificate while leaving global sign-chamber enumeration open.

body.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) allow arbitrary binary-path support, unit-specific known generalized propensities conditional on full potential-outcome schedules, non-identical units, and weak cross-unit dependence.  The new published-class theorem retains those features and the grand intercept in their equation \(4.2\), extends its probability-limit algebra to calendar-varying finite-memory effects, and recovers their Theorem \(4.1\) under homogeneity.  The separate i.i.d. conditional-mean identification class is incomparable overall and is not used as an inclusion argument.  Sun and Abraham (2021) decompose conventional event-study coefficients but do not study assignment-law reshaping of finite-memory lag regressors.  Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) motivate treatment-history indexing under known experimental assignment.  De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) recover time-constant random-coefficient distributed lags in complex designs.  Wright (2026) supplies adjacent public-manuscript evidence on conventional event-study diagnostics, and Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) supply modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients; none supplies the present tensor and ordered support geometry.
body.honest_scope: The proved forward algebra covers arbitrary finite binary-path supports.  Causal identification in the superpopulation layer requires consistency, pathwise conditional mean random assignment, overlap, the stated calendar-memory conditional mean, and full rank.  The separate estimator theorem covers the published unit-indexed known-propensity setup under Assumptions \(2.1\)--\(2.3\), with a grand intercept and no i.i.d. requirement.  Absorption is used only for the Green-kernel identity, graph-rank theorem, and adjacent-ratio certificate.  The graph dimension formula requires every reshaping mass to be positive and is false at the simplex boundary without deleting zero-mass paths.  The adjacent-ratio result is pointwise; global sign-chamber classification, inverse-image optimization, closest feasible target loading, and cross-fitted doubly robust inference are not claimed here.
